headline: Chip rally unwinds and the 10-year hits 5.14%; Nasdaq −0.9%, but S&P 500 ends week +2.5%
summary: Stocks opened higher after a softer-than-expected monthly PPI, then reversed within minutes as chipmakers gave back the week's post-Huang rally; the S&P 500 fell as much as 1.2% (low 7,499.40) and the Nasdaq about 1.8% before trimming losses into the close. Underneath it was a rotation rather than a rout: the equal-weight S&P 500 rose about 0.2%, seven of 11 sectors gained led by consumer staples (+1.4%), and the Dow edged up while tech (−2.0%) took the hit.
drivers: After a 10.6% surge over the first four days on bets Nvidia's rivals would gain, the SOX fell 3.4% as investors weighed Nvidia's role in funding the AI build-out: AMD −8.8% to $534 after a 45% five-day run, Sandisk −5.6%, Western Digital −5.0%, Broadcom −4.8% on a Redburn downgrade, Marvell −4.7% and Micron −2.5%. Nvidia slipped again for a sixth straight weekly loss (about −12% on the week, back below $4 trillion) as HSBC cut it to hold with a $170 target, and Arm fell 4.6% after an FT report that Nvidia's board approached its CEO Rene Haas.

Nebius fell 9.9% and CoreWeave 6.1% on a report that Microsoft is reviewing its neocloud contracts; Dell lost 7.2% after a report traced servers with restricted Nvidia chips to a Shanghai data center, and Treasury Secretary Bessent said Treasury had favored blacklisting Nvidia partner Megaspeed. Cisco dropped 6.2% as a squeeze in gross margin to 63.7% overshadowed record $18.5 billion revenue.
Wholesale inflation keeps hike bets intact

October PPI rose 0.3%, below the 0.4% forecast, but 6.5% from a year earlier, the most since November 2022; Fed Governor Bowman said hikes may be needed and Daly and Collins backed further tightening. The 10-year yield rose about 4bp to 5.14% (high 5.17%), the dollar index reached its highest since April 2025, and a December hike stays fully priced.

Consumer staples (+1.4%; PepsiCo +2.2%, Coca-Cola +1.9%), communication services (+1.1%, Meta +2.9%) and financials (+0.8%) cushioned the index. Modine jumped 28% on a report Samsung is in talks to buy the data-center cooling maker, Cerebras rose 11% after raising its 2026 outlook, and Nu Holdings gained 12% on record profit; airlines slipped late after an FAA nationwide ground stop.
week: For the week the S&P 500 rose 2.5% (its first weekly gain since early October), the Nasdaq 2.3% (best week since August), the Dow 2.1% and the Russell 2000 1.3%, even as Nvidia lost about 12% and the 10-year yield posted its biggest weekly jump since April 2025; WTI fell about 2.5% on the week as the IEA flagged a fourth-quarter supply surplus.
watch: Next: October retail sales and Nvidia's third-quarter results (its first under interim CEO Colette Kress) on Tue Nov 17, Palo Alto Networks results and Anthropic's IPO pricing on Wed Nov 18, and the Fed meeting on Dec 8–9.
